body:
Both scripts already take their single-instance lock inside
`_acquire_lock_or_exit()` rather than at import, so they avoid the test-poisoning
half of F-9032c8. Neither records the owning pid.

    lock = open(tempfile.gettempdir() + '/convert_library.lock', 'x')
    except FileExistsError: sys.exit(2)

Release is still `atexit.register(removeLock)`, which does not run on SIGKILL. So
a killed run still leaves a lock that blocks every later run of that service
until `cwa-init` sweeps `/tmp/*.lock` on the next container start.

User-visible shape: library conversion, or the Kindle EPUB fixer, silently stops
doing its job for the rest of the container's life, with only a log line saying
it "is already running" when nothing is.

PR #1510 fixed exactly this for `cover_enforcer.py` by recording the pid and
reclaiming the lock when that process is gone. The same helper shape applies
here; it was left out of #1510 to keep that change to one file.

Note `removeLock()` in both scripts is also an unguarded `os.remove`, which
raises at exit when cwa-init already swept the file.
title: convert_library and kindle_epub_fixer avoid the import-time lock but cannot reclaim one from a killed run
